config.title: Safe area insets

intro.title: Safe area insets
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple webpage header that adapts its padding to avoid overlapping with device notches or rounded corners. You will learn the core concept of safe area insets, which are CSS environment variables that provide dynamic spacing for modern device screens. The main technologies involved are the CSS `env()` function and the `safe-area-inset-*` variables. This will help you create designs that look great on all devices, from phones to tablets, by automatically adjusting for their unique screen shapes.
intro.usecase: Safe area insets are essential for creating mobile-friendly interfaces that adapt to device-specific features like notches, rounded corners, and home indicators. You'll use them in mobile apps and responsive websites to ensure content like navigation bars, bottom menus, and full-screen modals doesn't get obscured by these hardware elements. For example, in a mobile banking app, you'd apply safe area insets to keep transaction buttons and account balances visible on devices with notches, while in an e-commerce app, you'd use them to prevent product images from being clipped by rounded screen corners. This technique ensures your UI remains functional and visually consistent across all modern mobile devices.

objectives: Apply the env() function to access safe area inset values in CSS
Configure padding properties to accommodate device-specific safe areas
Implement safe area insets for both top and bottom viewport edges
Construct responsive layouts that adapt to different device notches and home indicators
Manipulate CSS custom properties to dynamically adjust safe area spacing
Integrate safe area insets with existing layout components
Control element positioning relative to device-specific viewport boundaries

steps.title: Create a CSS file and set up the viewport meta tag
steps.instruction: Create a new CSS file named 'styles.css' and ensure your HTML has the viewport meta tag with content='width=device-width, initial-scale=1'
steps.hint: In your HTML file, add <meta name='viewport' content='width=device-width, initial-scale=1'> inside the <head> section. Then create a separate CSS file named 'styles.css'.
steps.analogousExample:
/* HTML head section example */
<head>
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css">
</head>
steps.seedCode: /* Create your CSS file and add the viewport meta tag */
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a CSS file ready for styling and proper viewport configuration for responsive design.
successCriteria: A CSS file named 'styles.css' exists and the HTML contains the viewport meta tag with content='width=device-width, initial-scale=1'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you have both the CSS file and the viewport meta tag with exactly 'width=device-width, initial-scale=1'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you created 'styles.css' and added the viewport meta tag with content='width=device-width, initial-scale=1' to your HTML.

steps.title: Create a basic container with full viewport dimensions
steps.instruction: Create a CSS selector named .container that sets width to 100vw, height to 100vh, and background-color to lightblue.
steps.hint: Use the .container class selector and define the three properties: width, height, and background-color.
steps.expectedOutcome: A .container CSS rule is created with full viewport dimensions and a light blue background.
successCriteria: The .container selector has width: 100vw, height: 100vh, and background-color: lightblue.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure all three properties (width, height, background-color) are correctly set.
steps.feedbackWrong: The .container selector is missing or doesn't have the required properties. Try creating a .container class with width: 100vw, height: 100vh, and background-color: lightblue.

steps.title: Add content inside the container
steps.instruction: Inside the .container selector, add a new .content selector with padding: 20px, background: white, and text content.
steps.hint: Create a new CSS rule for .content that includes the specified properties and some text.
steps.expectedOutcome: A .content selector is added with the specified styles, creating a visual content area inside the container.
successCriteria: The .content selector exists with padding: 20px, background: white, and text content.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added the .content selector, but check if it has all the required properties: padding: 20px, background: white, and text content.
steps.feedbackWrong: The .content selector is missing or doesn't have the required properties. Review the instruction and try again.

steps.title: Introduce the env() function for safe-area-inset-top
steps.instruction: In the .container selector, add a padding-top property that uses the env() function with the safe-area-inset-top environment variable.
steps.hint: The env() function allows you to access device-specific environment variables. Use env(safe-area-inset-top) to get the top safe area inset value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .container selector now includes padding-top: env(safe-area-inset-top); to account for the top safe area.
successCriteria: The .container selector has padding-top: env(safe-area-inset-top); property added.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added padding-top: env(safe-area-inset-top); to the .container selector.
steps.feedbackWrong: The .container selector should include padding-top: env(safe-area-inset-top); to properly handle the top safe area.

steps.title: Add safe-area-inset-bottom to the container
steps.instruction: Add padding-bottom: env(safe-area-inset-bottom) to the .container selector to handle bottom safe areas for devices with home indicators.
steps.hint: Add the padding-bottom property with the env() function, similar to how you added padding-top.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .container selector now includes padding-bottom: env(safe-area-inset-bottom) to account for bottom safe areas.
successCriteria: The .container selector has padding-bottom: env(safe-area-inset-bottom) added.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added padding-bottom: env(safe-area-inset-bottom) to the .container selector.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't seem right. Add padding-bottom: env(safe-area-inset-bottom) to the .container selector.

steps.title: Apply safe-area-inset-left and safe-area-inset-right
steps.instruction: Add padding-left and padding-right properties to the .container selector, using env(safe-area-inset-left) and env(safe-area-inset-right) as their values.
steps.hint: Use the env() function with the safe-area-inset-left and safe-area-inset-right environment variables to set horizontal padding.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .container selector will have padding-left and padding-right properties set to the device's horizontal safe area insets.
successCriteria: The .container selector includes padding-left: env(safe-area-inset-left); and padding-right: env(safe-area-inset-right);
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure both padding-left and padding-right properties are added with the correct env() values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The horizontal safe area insets haven't been applied correctly. Check that you're using env(safe-area-inset-left) and env(safe-area-inset-right) for the padding properties.

steps.title: Create a header element that respects safe areas
steps.instruction: Create a CSS selector named .header with padding that uses env(safe-area-inset-top) for the top padding and sets left/right padding to 20px, and give it a darkblue background color.
steps.hint: The padding property can take multiple values: top, right, bottom, left. Use env(safe-area-inset-top) for the top value, then set the right and left values.
steps.expectedOutcome: A .header CSS rule is added with padding that respects the top safe area and has a dark blue background.
successCriteria: The .header selector exists with padding: env(safe-area-inset-top) 20px 20px and background: darkblue.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the .header selector has both the correct padding values and the darkblue background.
steps.feedbackWrong: The .header selector is missing or doesn't match the required properties. Check the padding and background values.

steps.title: Create a footer with bottom safe area handling
steps.instruction: Create a CSS selector for a footer element with class 'footer' that uses env(safe-area-inset-bottom) for its bottom padding.
steps.hint: Add a new .footer selector with padding that includes the safe area inset at the bottom.
steps.expectedOutcome: A footer selector is added that will handle bottom device intrusions using safe-area-inset-bottom.
successCriteria: The .footer selector exists with padding that includes env(safe-area-inset-bottom).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a footer, but make sure it uses env(safe-area-inset-bottom) in its padding.
steps.feedbackWrong: The footer selector is missing or doesn't properly handle the bottom safe area.

steps.title: Use min() function as fallback for safe area values
steps.instruction: Update the .container's padding-top rule to use min(env(safe-area-inset-top), 20px) as a fallback value.
steps.hint: The min() function takes two values and uses the smaller one. This ensures that if safe-area-inset-top is not supported, the padding will default to 20px.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .container will have a fallback padding of 20px if the safe-area-inset-top environment variable is not supported by the browser.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the min() function correctly with env(safe-area-inset-top) and 20px as arguments.
steps.feedbackWrong: The .container's padding-top rule should use min(env(safe-area-inset-top), 20px) to provide a fallback value.

steps.title: Test with different device orientations
steps.instruction: Add a media query for landscape orientation that adjusts the container's safe area padding values.
steps.hint: Use @media (orientation: landscape) to target landscape mode, then override the padding properties inside the container selector.
steps.expectedOutcome: The CSS will include a media query that adjusts safe area padding when the device is in landscape orientation.
successCriteria: A media query for landscape orientation is added and contains adjustments to the container's padding properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a media query, but make sure it targets landscape orientation and adjusts the container's padding properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The media query for landscape orientation is missing or incorrect. Review the instruction and try again.
